The Brief

BOHRAI is not an event. It is the operational fabric beneath India's deep-tech transition.

Position

India does not lack ambitious technologists. What it has lacked is a coherent national surface — a place where serious work in AI, robotics and silicon can be evaluated, validated and routed to the missions that need it.

BOHRAI is an initiative under Pure AI Global — designed as that surface. It connects every level of the deep-tech economy, from a student soldering their first board to a venture-backed company preparing its first industrial pilot, through one disciplined, peer-reviewed pathway.

The platform is deliberately institution-agnostic. What matters is the technology, the team's seriousness, and a demonstrated route from prototype to deployment. Every submission moves through the same evaluation engine; every track is anchored to specific national missions, industrial applications and a clear destination beyond the showroom.

"Treat deep technology as national infrastructure — not as a product category."

— Pure AI Global · founding brief

Innovator-owned, always. Intellectual property remains with its creators. Pure AI Global takes no equity and no royalty as a condition of participation. Commercialization partnerships are optional and separately negotiated.

Conducted By
The parent organisation. Pure AI Global builds sovereign AI-native infrastructure, autonomous systems and deep-tech networks designed to serve the long-term interests of Bharat.
Vision

To build sovereign AI-native ecosystems, intelligent infrastructures, autonomous systems and deep-tech innovation networks that serve the long-term interests of Bharat.

To connect students, startups, researchers, industry leaders and government innovation programmes into a single, coherent national acceleration platform — one that treats deep technology as infrastructure rather than as a product category.

Initiative hierarchy & operating layers
Openness

What makes BOHRAI open.

Openness here is structural — built into who can participate, how submissions move through the system, and where the work eventually lands.

01 · Participation

Open to every builder.

Students, faculty, independent researchers, makers, university labs and early-stage startups — admitted on the basis of work, not institution.

02 · Innovation

Cross-domain by design.

AI, robotics, drones, semiconductors, healthcare, autonomous systems and manufacturing automation evaluated as one interconnected surface.

03 · Ecosystem

Connected to the real economy.

Integrated with government missions, incubators, investors, academia and manufacturing ecosystems through standing partnerships.

04 · Commercialization

From prototype to deployment.

Pathways into startups, industrial pilots, research collaborations and venture-backed deep-tech companies are mapped, not implied.

Pipeline

From innovation to national deployment.

An eight-stage pipeline, designed so that every submission has a defined path forward — including the explicit option to exit at any stage with full ownership intact.

Stage 01

Innovation Submission

Open intake of functional prototypes, working systems and pre-production technologies across all tracks.

Stage 02

Technical Evaluation

Peer-reviewed assessment by domain panels drawn from academia, industry and applied research.

Stage 03

Pure AI Validation Sandbox

Hands-on validation inside controlled testbeds — performance, reliability, manufacturability.

Stage 04

Mentorship & Engineering Sprints

Targeted technical depth, engineering reviews and structured sprints with senior practitioners.

Stage 05

Government Mission Alignment

Routing to the national missions whose mandate, infrastructure and funding best fit the work.

Stage 06

Incubation & Startup Transition

Structured incorporation, founding support and incubator placement for ventures that choose that path.

Stage 07

Investor & Industry Connect

Curated introductions to deep-tech funds, strategic acquirers and industrial pilot customers.

Stage 08

National Scale-Up & Deployment

Production-grade deployment with industry partners, government programmes or strategic missions.

Tracks

Eight sovereign technology tracks.

Tracks are scoped narrowly enough to evaluate seriously and broadly enough to admit unexpected work. Each is anchored to specific national missions, industrial applications and deployment pathways.

Track 01 · Featured

Next-Gen AI & Autonomous Agents

Agentic systems, reasoning agents, multi-agent orchestration and sovereign foundation-model applications — evaluated for deployment readiness, not benchmark performance.

Track 02 · Featured

Industry 4.0 Robotics & Smart Manufacturing

Industrial robotics, factory automation, digital twins and manufacturing intelligence systems — with direct routing to MSME and SAMARTH industrial pilot programmes.

Track 03

Drones & Aerial
Autonomous Systems

Track 04

Track 05

Intellectual Property

Innovator-owned. Always.

100%Innovator-Owned IP

You build it. You own it. There is no asterisk.

BOHRAI is an open national platform — the integrity of that promise depends on a clear, unambiguous position on intellectual property. The terms are short on purpose.

  • ✓Participants retain full ownership of their intellectual property, code, designs and underlying technology.
  • ✓Pure AI Global claims zero equity as a condition of participation, mentorship or validation support.
  • ✓No royalty extraction. No future revenue-share. No silent claims on derivative work.
  • ✓Commercialization partnerships are optional, separately negotiated, and only entered when the innovator chooses.
Common Questions

Things people actually ask.

Q · 01Who is eligible to participate in BOHRAI?+
Participation is open to students, faculty, independent researchers, makers and early-stage startups — across institutions and geographies in India. The platform is institution-agnostic by design; what matters is the quality and seriousness of the work.
Q · 02Does Pure AI Global take any equity, royalty or IP rights?+
No. Participants retain full ownership of their intellectual property. Pure AI Global takes zero equity and zero royalty as a condition of participation. Commercialization partnerships are optional and separately negotiated.
Q · 03Is BOHRAI an operating system or a software platform?+
No. BOHRAI is an initiative — a national innovation platform under Pure AI Global. It coordinates evaluation, validation and mission-routing for India's deep-tech ecosystem. It is not an OS or a product.
Q · 04What funding and infrastructure pathways are available?+
Selected work is routed to relevant government innovation missions, deep-tech funds, incubators and industry partners. Specific instruments — grants, pilot funding, seed capital — depend on the track and the readiness stage.
Q · 05How is BOHRAI aligned with national programmes?+
Tracks are mapped explicitly to existing national missions including IndiaAI, the Semiconductor Mission, iDEX, NIDHI PRAYAS, the National Quantum Mission and others. Alignment happens at the design stage so that promising work has a clear destination.
Q · 06What does a strong submission look like?+
A functional prototype or working system, accompanied by a clear articulation of the problem, technical approach and intended deployment context. Polish matters less than evidence that the technology actually works and that the team understands where it goes next.
Q · 07How are submissions evaluated?+
Peer-reviewed by domain panels drawn from academia, industry and applied research. Evaluation criteria centre on technical depth, manufacturability, sovereign relevance and commercial viability.
Q · 08Can an industry or government body partner with BOHRAI?+
Yes. The platform is structured to host long-term partnerships — corporate challenges, pilot programmes, recruitment pipelines, joint research and mission alignment. Partnership formats are tailored to the partner's needs.
